picked.t: Japan looks to Bangladesh, Nepal for farmhands as Vietnamese recruiters struggle to fill jobs
picked.body: Tokyo-based Mirai, which trains and places skilled foreign workers, has introduced its first Bangladeshi candidates for farm work, Kyodo News reported. Two students from one of its partner schools in Bangladesh passed Japan's specified skilled worker agriculture exam in August and received job offers from an agricultural company in northeastern Aomori Prefecture, where they are due to head in the coming months. "I am very excited to go to Japan and learn about Japanese agriculture," Ahasan Habib, 21, from Mymensingh in northern Bangladesh, told the Japanese news site. "I want to make good use of my experience and take proper care of chickens." The other candidate, Siam Ur Rahman, 20, from Barisal in southern Bangladesh, said he wanted "to work very hard" in Japan and was looking forward to touching snow. The two will join Japan's Type 1 specified skilled workers in agriculture, whose stays are generally capped at five years. Their number rose 26% from a year earlier to 44,050 at the end of June, according to the Immigration Services Agency. Indonesia remained the largest supplier with 18,255 farm workers, up 45%, followed by Vietnam with 10,261, up 11%. Vietnam's share of the sector fell from about 26% a year earlier to 23%, although it is still the largest source of Type 1 workers across all fields, with 163,154 of the 425,961 in Japan. South Asian farm workers numbers remain small but are climbing fast. Bangladesh's count jumped 127% to 334, Sri Lanka's climbed 60% to 638 and Nepal's rose 30% to 916. Yuji Nomura, general manager of the career advisory division at Mirai's parent company Sustainable Holdings, told Kyodo News that rising wages in Vietnam, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries were making it harder for Japan to attract farm workers from there. "We're seeing a shift to South Asia for labor supply sources," he said. To qualify for specified skilled worker status in agriculture, candidates should pass the N4 beginner-level Japanese test as well as written and practical farming exams, Nomura said. Sustainable Holdings runs Mirai partner schools in the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and has added schools in Sri Lanka and Nepal. Japan's farms face chronic labor shortages due to aging and other factors. Including technical intern trainees, 67,905 foreigners held specified skilled worker or trainee status in agriculture at the end of 2025, according to government data. Noriyuki Takakura, a director at Sustainable Holdings, said workers from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal were highly regarded for their seriousness and diligence. The company offers free tuition at Mirai partner schools across Asia and helps students find housing in Japan. "We will gradually expand agricultural classes in each country," Takakura said. In Vietnam, Japan was the top destination for workers going abroad in 2025, receiving more than 64,600, but it has slipped to second place this year. Of the 114,276 Vietnamese who left to work overseas on contracts in the first 10 months, 50,473 went to Taiwan and 45,658 to Japan, according to the Department of Overseas Labor Management. Pham Van Trong, human resources manager at a Hanoi company that has sent workers to Japan for more than a decade, including in agriculture, told VnExpress that each job order once drew seven or eight applicants but now gets about two per position. The company's supply of candidates has fallen about 60%, he said. Trong said more jobs at home were part of the reason, with unskilled construction work now paying around VND20 million ($770). But he blamed mainly the weaker yen, which once fetched VND200-220 and now fetches about VND160-170. Workers' total incomes are 1.2 to 1.5 times what they were a decade ago, but their savings have not kept pace. On VND30-40 million ($1,150-1,540) a month, they used to send home VND20-25 million ($770-960), and they still send about the same. "With the yen sliding and savings not growing, workers will think twice," Trong said.

picked.t: Inside Binh Tay, the 96-year-old Chinatown market in HCMC
picked.body: Binh Tay Market is situated between Thap Muoi, Le Tan Ke, Phan Van Khoe, and Tran Binh streets in Binh Tay Ward, an area with a large Hoa community, people of Chinese ancestry. Besides serving locals, the market is a regular stop for tourists visiting HCMC. According to Nguyen Thi Ngoc Chau, deputy director of the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market was built in 1930. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. The market, which was renovated in 2016, retains its original architecture. It spreads over 25,000 square meters with a floor area of more than 17,000 square meters, and has one main gate and 12 side entrances. It has a tall tower with four clock faces. The yin-yang tiled roofs are arranged in overlapping layers and curve upward at the corners. In 2017, the market was recognized as a city architectural and artistic heritage site. In 2022, it was named a tourist attraction of HCMC. According to Le Hong Minh, head of the business management team at the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market has 2,358 stalls that sell more than 30 product categories. Its main goods include spices, groceries, clothing, and confectionery. Data from 2023 to 2026 shows that 73% of visitors to the market are international. It receives 120,000 foreign visitors a year, most of them brought on guided tours. On Sept. 8, a group of 10 Indian tourists led by Rohan and his wife spent over an hour exploring the market and buying more than a dozen handmade bags as gifts. Rohan praised its architecture and range of goods but said the products were similar to those at other markets in town. Stalls selling dry goods and spices are located near the market's main gate. Minh said shopping preferences at Binh Tay vary by region. European and American tourists buy handicrafts and clothing. Southeast Asian visitors shop for confectionery, tea, coffee, and bamboo goods. Northeast Asian tourists prefer specialties, dried foods, and herbal medicines. Besides shopping, the market has a food area serving dishes from all over Vietnam. Binh Tay Market plans to combine shopping with cultural and culinary experiences by offering heritage tours, spiritual visits, performances recreating old Chinatown, craft workshops with artisans, and Chinese-Vietnamese cuisine. picked.t: Vietnamese woman wins over Brazilian parents-in-law with traditional dishes made from local ingredients
picked.body: In late October, while visiting a park in the state of Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, she cut a few wild banana leaves to bring home and wrap banh tet (Vietnamese sticky rice cake), one of her husband’s favorite Vietnamese dishes. To help him and his parents like Vietnamese food, the 36-year-old from southern Dong Nai province had earlier spent two years overcoming numerous challenges and ingredient shortages. She had met her husband, a doctor, when he came to HCMC on a vacation. They dated and got married in 2019, after which she moved to Rio de Janeiro with him. At first, she struggled to adapt to the local cuisine. Brazilian meals primarily consist of loose, long-grain rice served with black beans stewed and salted meat, and consist of very few brothy soups. Thuy craved Vietnamese noodles and pickled vegetables, but it was very difficult to find Vietnamese ingredients. There were only two stores in Rio de Janeiro selling Asian ingredients such as fish sauce, tofu, fermented tofu, and rice paper, and the store closest to her house was a 45-minute drive away. By late 2020, when she was pregnant with her first child, Natalia, her craving for Vietnamese dishes had grown even stronger, and she began thinking about how to cook some of them using locally available ingredients. She thinly sliced cucumbers and carrots, and tossed them with salt, garlic, and chili to make quick pickles. She also bought mung beans and sprouted them to get fresh bean sprouts. Noticing that locals ate a lot of fish and local markets sold okra, pineapple, and tomatoes, she used these ingredients to make canh chua ca (Vietnamese sour fish soup). Her parents-in-law were surprised the first time they saw a bowl of fish and vegetable soup, as Brazilians are used to eating grilled fish or pan-seared fillets. However, after taking a spoonful of the broth, they were amazed at how the mild sourness from the pineapple and tomatoes completely eliminated any fishy odor. "After my daughter was born, I wanted her and the whole family to get to know and love Vietnamese food," Thuy says. With that goal in mind, she decided to transform her in-laws' palates. Thuy's husband has been a vegetarian for many years, but vegetarian diets in Brazil can be quite monotonous as local food usually features fatty meats. Even traditional stewed black beans are typically simmered with salted meat, leaving vegetarians with few choices beyond plain white rice, boiled cassava, or lettuce salads. Thuy bought tofu, mushrooms, rice vermicelli, and rice paper from the Asian stores, and combined them with tomatoes and carrots from local markets to create vegetarian dishes. She made fried tofu in tomato sauce, mushrooms braised in pepper sauce, stir-fried rice vermicelli with vegetables, and vegetarian summer rolls served with peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. While hiking in the mountains, she noticed clumps of wild bamboo shoots, which locals do not eat since they regard them as just another forest plant. Thuy dug up the shoots, peeled them, boiled them multiple times to remove the bitterness, and stir-fried them with garlic or cooked them in soup. When Thuy’s husband saw her bring home wild bamboo shoots from the forest and season them with garlic and chili, he hesitated at first. However, after trying a bite of the stir-fry, he was surprised by its crisp texture and delicate sweetness. He finished the entire plate in one sitting and immediately fell in love with the dish. In Brazil, jackfruits grow abundantly along roadsides and in parks, but locals don’t eat them and simply let ripe jackfruits fall to the ground. Thuy once picked an unripe jackfruit, trimmed off the peel full of sap, boiled it until tender, and used half to make shredded jackfruit salad and braised the other half in black pepper sauce. Because Vietnamese herbs were hard to find, she substituted peppermint for Vietnamese mint. Her husband took a bite and was amazed by the chewy, nutty texture of the shredded jackfruit that was infused with garlic and chili. "The dish feels light on the stomach and isn't heavy or greasy," he says. He asks his wife to cook Vietnamese food three times every week now. Thuy's parents-in-law live on their own and occasionally visit their son’s family. In the beginning, the difference in eating habits would lead to many awkward situations. Once, while she was braising pork ribs, the pungent smell of fish sauce filled the kitchen, and it alarmed her in-laws so much that they flung open the windows and took refuge in the living room. When she craved pickled mustard greens during her pregnancy, her husband drove nearly an hour to buy the greens for her to pickle. After seeing white foam forming in the jar and the greens changing color, her mother-in-law told her son to throw the pickles away. "I was heartbroken over the wasted batch, but I figured they were only worried because they cared about their daughter-in-law," Thuy says. picked.t: 8 tidal gates shield Ho Chi Minh City streets from flooding
picked.body: Tran Xuan Soan Street in former District 7 remained dry at 5:30 p.m., despite being a regular flooding hotspot whenever water levels in nearby rivers and canals rise. Just a month earlier, a stretch of more than 3 km of the road was submerged, with floodwaters reaching halfway up vehicle wheels and forcing many commuters to push their motorbikes through the water. The road's protection from flooding is attributed to the newly completed VND10 trillion (US$387 million) tidal control system. At noon on Wednesday, project investor Trung Nam Group lowered the sluice gates, closing all eight tidal control structures at the mouths of major rivers in the city's urban core. The system has helped reduce high-tide flooding in several areas in the city's south, including parts of the former districts 1, 7 and 8, and Nha Be District. The project is expected to mitigate flooding across 570 sq.km of the inner city, equivalent to one-fourth of the city’s land area before the merger, benefiting approximately 6.5 million people. picked.t: Nutifood forms US nutrition science alliance with four partners
picked.body: Nutifood announced the establishment of Nutifood American Nutrition Science in Kansas on Nov. 24. The new entity will connect the company's research and product development capabilities with the U.S. nutrition science, dairy ingredients, and manufacturing sectors. The launch was marked by a signing ceremony with Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), witnessed by representatives of the Vietnamese Consulate General in San Francisco and senior U.S. dairy industry executives. Building on a scientific foundation The move builds on Nutifood's more than 25 years of research and development (R&D) experience across Vietnam, Sweden, and Australia, where it has developed nutrition solutions for different consumer needs. In early 2026, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted a patent for the company's proprietary FDI formula, expanding its intellectual property portfolio. The U.S. offers an opportunity for Nutifood to tap into an advanced dairy ecosystem spanning ingredients, manufacturing, research, and clinical science. Through its new entity, the company aims to combine its intellectual property and research expertise with U.S. scientific and industrial resources, moving beyond conventional exports to participate more deeply in the nutrition value chain. Four U.S. partners Nutifood is forming a Nutrition Science Alliance with the California Milk Advisory Board (CMAB), California Dairies, Inc. (CDI), DFA, and Natural Immune Systems Laboratories (NIS Labs). Each partner brings different capabilities: CMAB connects the company with California's dairy industry and products bearing the Real California Milk seal; CDI provides large-scale dairy processing and manufacturing; DFA contributes R&D and formula innovation; and NIS Labs offers laboratory testing, preclinical studies, and human research. By combining these capabilities across ingredients, manufacturing, R&D, and clinical research, Nutifood aims to improve control over product development and meet scientific and quality standards in international markets. "Every age group, body condition, and stage of life requires specialized nutrition solutions grounded in scientific evidence. That is why Nutifood American Nutrition Science is not simply looking for ingredient suppliers or manufacturing facilities in the United States," said Tran Bao Minh, vice chairman of Nutifood. "We are building strategic partnerships with CMAB, CDI, DFA, and NIS Labs to combine advanced technology and research capabilities in order to develop new nutrition standards for consumers worldwide." Through its U.S. entity and four strategic partnerships, Nutifood aims to strengthen its international competitiveness by combining its research capabilities and patented technologies with American scientific and manufacturing resources.

picked.t: Vietnam makes unprecedented commitments in US trade talks: ministry
picked.body: He spoke at a ministry press conference on the preliminary findings of the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) in its investigation into industrial overcapacity. The U.S. released findings for 14 of the 16 economies under investigation, Vietnam included, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which targets unfair trade practices. President Donald Trump's administration has proposed new tariffs of 15-35% on these partners. Chu Thang Trung, acting director of the ministry's Trade Remedies Authority, said the USTR has proposed an additional tariff of up to 35% on Vietnam. The rate is only a proposal, has not taken effect and could fall to 20% if the two countries reach an Agreement on Reciprocal, Fair and Balanced Trade (ART). The final rate will depend on information the parties provide, the outcome of consultations and progress in Vietnam-U.S. negotiations, he added. Thai said Vietnam is working with the U.S. through two parallel channels. The first is taking full part in the U.S. investigation, including supplying information, submitting written rebuttals and attending public hearings. The ministry has prepared comments to send to U.S. investigators. The second is negotiating the reciprocal trade agreement, in which Vietnam has offered commitments that match, and in some areas exceed, those in all the free trade agreements (FTAs) it has signed. "Vietnam has put forward commitments at the highest possible level, showing maximum effort in the negotiations, including commitments that are unprecedented," he said. Thai added that the investigated countries he had spoken with on the sidelines of international conferences all disagreed with the overcapacity allegations behind the tariffs. On Wednesday, just before the U.S. released its preliminary report, Permanent Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc met with ministries and agencies to discuss risk management measures. On the reciprocal trade talks, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Pham Thu Hang told a press conference the same day that the two sides have largely agreed on the content. "Only a few technical issues remain to be discussed and clarified before the negotiations are completed," she said. In July, the U.S. began collecting new tariffs on 60 economies over imports of products made with forced labor, with Vietnam facing a rate of 12.5%. Thai said Washington has yet to decide how tariffs from the two investigations will be applied. "They have also not decided whether the two tariffs will be stacked or merged," he said, adding that the U.S. plans to weigh the tariffs as a whole after taking in the parties' views during consultations. Vietnam also faces a Section 301 investigation into intellectual property, handled by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The U.S. has extended that probe, and it is unclear when preliminary findings will be released. Thai said Vietnam has made considerable efforts to enforce intellectual property rules and has joined new-generation FTAs with high standards in the field, so it hopes the U.S. will not impose tariffs when the investigation ends. Amid the shifts in trade policy, the ministry advised businesses to draw up their own risk management plans suited to each product group. Under the preliminary overcapacity findings, the USTR proposed exempting 2,021 tariff lines, including some Vietnamese exports such as tea and coffee. Products covered by Section 232, the national security tariffs on steel, aluminum and cars, may also be spared the additional Section 301 duties in line with recent U.S. practice, meaning risk levels will vary across sectors, the ministry said. It urged companies to watch for warnings on tariff evasion, diversify their markets and consult the government's 2026-2030 overall plan for managing the trade surplus to head off risks. Despite the complex international trade environment, Vietnam's total import-export turnover is expected to hit a record of more than $1.2 trillion this year, exceeding its target, Thai said.

picked.t: Vietnam has strong potential to attract billions in foreign capital: experts
picked.body: Experts shared these views at the HDBank Global Capital Conference 2026, themed "Global Capital – Vietnam's Aspirations," which brought together nearly 1,000 delegates in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi on Wednesday. Attendees included Philipp Rösler, vice chairman of HD Securities; Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, chairwoman of Sovico Group; Kim Byoungho, chairman of HDBank; and Darryl James Dong, former head of the International Finance Corporation's (IFC) office in Ho Chi Minh City, along with financial executives, experts and domestic and international investors. Golden opportunity to attract foreign capital Speaking at the conference, Rösler said Vietnam would need approximately $1.5 trillion in investment to achieve double-digit growth from 2026 to 2030, while the state budget could cover only about 20% of the total. This highlights the need to develop domestic capital markets and expand access to international funding. "Capital does not fear risk, but it always fears uncertainty," he said. Capital can move worldwide in search of growth, Rösler said, but stays only where rules are clear, information is transparent and commitments are honored. FTSE Russell's upgrade of Vietnam's stock market and the launch of the Vietnam International Financial Center are complementary milestones. To capitalize on them, he called for consistent and predictable policies, gradual market opening and compliance with international corporate governance standards. From a banking perspective, Kim Byoungho said Vietnam's integration into global financial markets should rest on three pillars: capital, standards and partnerships. HDBank, Sovico and their partners are expanding cooperation in London, New York, Tokyo, Singapore and Seoul to broaden fundraising opportunities and support Vietnamese companies' international expansion. Thomas Nguyen, a senior international stock market expert, said the upgrade would make Vietnam's stock market more accessible to foreign investors. However, attracting global capital remains challenging as much of investors' attention is currently focused on artificial intelligence and technology. He identified four potential drivers of Vietnam's stock market growth in 2027: increased foreign inflows following the upgrade, infrastructure reforms, possible shifts in global capital as the AI investment boom cools, and lower deposit interest rates. Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao said Vietnam's ability to implement programs and projects quickly was a key advantage. She cited the resolution of trading system congestion at the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange within 90 days using domestic technology, and an online platform that raised more than $400 million for the Covid-19 vaccine fund. She also stressed the importance of reliable local partners and regulatory support in investment decisions. Thao said investors who participated in Vietjet's initial public offering (IPO) have seen their investments increase more than fivefold, while those who bought HDBank shares in its 2018 IPO have gained approximately sixfold. She said both companies have maintained commitments to transparency, corporate governance and long-term value creation. Vietnam also has significant investment potential in infrastructure, technology, education, healthcare, culture and human development, she said. "I hope investors, particularly international investors, will seize the opportunities offered by Vietnam's capital market, build a better future for themselves, and grow alongside this market," she added. Gateways connecting Vietnam with global investment markets A highlight of the conference was a bell-ringing ceremony marking the IPO of HD Securities Joint Stock Company (HDS), which has a valuation of nearly $1.8 billion. Representatives of regulators, HDBank and HD Securities joined the ceremony at the HCMC and Hanoi venues. HD Securities Chairman Vu Huu Dien said the company aims to become one of Vietnam's three largest securities firms by 2030 and lead the market in smart trading platforms and AI-powered governance. It also plans to establish a securities subsidiary at the Vietnam International Financial Center. CEO Nguyen Ha Quynh said HD Securities is focusing on four business areas: investment banking, securities brokerage and margin lending, treasury operations, and investment and proprietary trading. The company aims to raise shareholders' equity to VND77-78 trillion ($3 million) by 2030 while maintaining a return on equity above 20%. Its IPO is expected to raise VND4.737 trillion ($183.38 million), with 60% allocated to margin lending, 30% to financial instrument investments and the remainder to other business activities. During a question-and-answer session, Tran Hoai Nam, standing deputy CEO of HDBank, said the bank aims to raise at least $2 billion annually from international sources. picked.t: 잘나가던 베트남 대표 택시社 마이린, 차량호출 경쟁 심화에 ‘채무불이행’ 맞아
picked.body: 베트남 택시회사 마이린의 택시차량들. (사진=doanhnghiephoinhap) 한때 비나선(Vinasun)과 함께 베트남 대표 택시 업체로 군림했던 마이린(Mai Linh)이 극심한 재정난 속에 채무불이행으로 부동산 담보 자산이 압류되는 사태를 맞았다. 베트남 시중은행 중 하나인 LP은행(LPBank)은 최근 마이린그룹의 계열사 마이린호이안(Mai Linh Hoi An)의 담보자산 압류 계획을 자사 홈페이지에 공고했다. 공고문에 따르면, 압류 대상 담보물은 707㎡ 규모 필지의 토지사용권과 해당 부지 내 시설물이다. 베트남에서 땅은 원칙적으로 국가 소유로, 토지를 사용할 권리인 토지사용권이 담보물로 사용된다. LP은행은 “그동안 미상환 채무 회수를 위해 마이린그룹과 마이린호이안에 담보물 인도를 요청해왔으나, 두 회사가 이에 응하지 않음에 따라 압류 절차를 진행하기로 결정했다”고 설명했다. 마이린은 비나선과 함께 베트남에서 가장 오래된 택시 브랜드 가운데 하나로, 차량 전체를 녹색으로 도장한 것이 가장 큰 특징이다. 마이린을 포함한 전통 택시 업체들은 최근 수년간 그랩과 그린GSM(Green Sm), 비(be) 등 기술 기반 차량호출 플랫폼 시장이 급격한 성장세를 보이면서 극심한 타격을 받고 있다. 마이린그룹 직원 수 또한 큰 폭으로 줄었는데, 이 또한 지난 몇 년간 플랫폼 사업자들과의 경쟁이 격화된 데 따른 것으로 풀이된다. 호치민시 사업자등록국에 따르면, 11월 현재 공식 등록된 마이린그룹 직원 수는 120명에 불과했다. 앞서 5월 갱신 당시 재직 규모가 5,500명 안팎이었던 것을 감안하면 전체 97.8%가 줄어든 수준이다. 다만, 신고된 인원 수는 마이린그룹이라는 등록 법인에 한정된 숫자여서 마이린 생태계 전체의 직원 수를 온전히 반영하지는 않는다. 한편 마이린그룹은 신고 인원이 이렇게 크게 바뀐 이유에 대해 별다른 입장을 내놓지 않고 있다.

picked.t: South Korea's passport slips to third place, trailing Japan and UAE
picked.body: Previously, it shared second place with Japan and the UAE, both of which retain their positions in the latest ranking with visa-free access to 188 destinations. Singapore continues holding the world's most powerful passport, allowing visa-free entry to 193 destinations. The U.S. passport rose one spot to ninth in the index, with visa-free access increasing from 179 to 180 destinations. Vietnam's passport has climbed four places to 85th as its holders can enter 50 destinations worldwide without obtaining a visa in advance. The five weakest passports belong to Pakistan, Yemen, Iraq, Syria, and Afghanistan. The Henley Passport Index tracks global travel freedom across 227 countries and territories, using data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA). It ranks 199 passports based on the number of destinations their holders can enter without obtaining a visa in advance. Updated regularly throughout the year to reflect changes in visa policies, the index is widely regarded as a key measure of global mobility.
